answer.rationale: A: a subgroup meta-analysis finds short-term LCD effective for weight loss versus a normal or high carbohydrate diet (WMD -1.18, 95% CI -2.32 to -0.04, P=0.04). The extracted 'lower' direction matches the negative WMD, read as greater weight loss with LCD, although the rendered sentence 'weight loss was lower' is awkward. B: across RCTs of at least 3 months, change in weight did not differ significantly between LCD and HCD. Extraction gaps are not material: A's context omits the 'short term' duration; B leaves both groups unnamed and marks author significance as not reported although the abstract says 'did not differ significantly'. Exposure, outcome and between-diet comparison are the same; A reports an effect and B does not confirm it. A's own conclusion reports no significant effect on long-term weight loss, so intervention duration is a visible difference. Both are meta-analyses of RCTs and may share trials, which the abstracts do not let me check.
answer.label: not_replicated

answer.rationale: A: the meta-analysis reports lower body weight with TRE than controls (-0.48 kg, 95% CI -0.74 to -0.22, P < .01) and calls the reduction significant. B: the selected finding is a secondary one, the per-protocol difference after the 3-month post-intervention follow-up (-0.4 kg, -1.8 to 1.0), described as not maintained. The trial concludes there was no clinically relevant effect on bodyweight (intention-to-treat -0.8 kg, p=0.099), although per-protocol at the end of intervention showed -1.0 kg (p=0.040). Extraction omissions do not change either finding: in A the aims, group names and comparator field are empty although the abstract gives them; in B the 10-h per-day eating window is not recorded as dose. B's time point is post-intervention follow-up while A gives none; I treated both as TRE-versus-control bodyweight contrasts, so the pair is effect versus not confirmed. Whether the meta-analysis includes this trial cannot be seen from the abstracts.
